text:
alex: thinking about adding queue reservation + TTL smoothing on ingest to dampen cost spikes from late enrichment fanout. quick gut check?

maria: yep, we've been seeing those bursts. backlog drains and then a huge fanout kills throughput and bill.

chris: rough idea: reserve N slots per tenant (configurable) and release extra capacity gradually across a smoothing_window (eg 5m). prevents all-backlog-draining at once.

alex: ok but that wastes reserved capacity during normal ops. tradeoff between wasted GPUs vs avoiding momentary mega-bursts. any metric ideas to tune N?

sam: track three metrics: `queue_util_pct`, `reserved_unused_pct`, and `drain_rate`. Also capture `fanout_events_per_min`. use those to auto-tune reservation.

chris: proto config snippet:```yaml
ingest:
  queue_reservation:
    enabled: true
    per_tenant: 50
    smoothing_window: 5m
    release_step: 5
```

maria: edge case — multi-tenant super-bursts. maybe we need priority eviction (SLA-based) so high-SLA tenants can preempt soft-reserved slots. ties into billing-key propagation.

alex: agree. canary plan: roll to us-west; monitor p50/p95 latency and reserved_unused. abort if p95 increases > 200ms or reserved_unused > 80% for 10m.

ingest-bot: deploy scheduled: canary-reservation-v1 -> us-west (tomorrow 10:00 UTC) :rocket:

chris: i'll update the RFC with the smoothing algorithm and add perf test plans. want a perf harness run against staging? @maria

maria: yes please — i'll add dashboard cards (reserved_unused, queue_util, drain_rate) + an alert if reserved_unused > 70% for 10m.

alex: sweet. i'll file the follow-up RFC and assign owners. link will be posted here once done. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
